text:
Mercedes-Benz Stadium broke ground on mayo 19, 2014, and opened on agosto 26, 2017, in downtown Atlanta, replacing the Georgia Dome. Built at a construction cost of approximately US$1.6 billion (a 2016 estimate), it was conceived as a state-of-the-art home for the city's professional football. It is owned by the Georgia World Congress Center Authority and operated by AMB Sports and Entertainment Group under owner Arthur Blank.

The design was led by 360 Architecture, an HOK subsidiary, working alongside tvsdesign, Goode Van Slyke Architecture, and Stanley Beaman & Sears. Its signature feature is a retractable roof built from eight translucent triangular "pinwheel," camera-aperture panels that open and close above the bowl. The venue's permanent playing surface is FieldTurf CORE artificial turf.

Since 2017, Mercedes-Benz Stadium has served as the home of the NFL's Atlanta Falcons and MLS's Atlanta United FC, with an Atlanta NWSL team slated to begin play in 2028. From the outset it was designed to host the biggest events in American sport. It staged Super Bowl LIII on febrero 3, 2019, where the Patriots beat the Rams 13-3, and it hosted the 2018 and 2025 College Football Playoff National Championships. The stadium is set to host Super Bowl LXII in 2028.

The venue carries a genuine football lineage as well, having hosted the 2018 MLS Cup and two 2024 Copa America matches. For the 2026 World Cup it takes the name Atlanta Stadium and welcomes eight matches: five group-stage fixtures, one Round of 32, one Round of 16, and a semi-final on julio 15, 2026 — its largest tournament responsibility yet.
